title: The Mary Celeste
hook: In 1872, a ship was found sailing the Atlantic with nobody on board.

beats.label: THE CASE
beats.line: The Mary Celeste was spotted drifting, sails set, with no one at the wheel.

beats.label: CLUE 1
beats.line: Below deck, six months of food and water sat untouched.

beats.label: CLUE 2
beats.line: The only lifeboat was gone, and the captain's log ended ten days earlier.

beats.label: CLUE 3
beats.line: Her cargo: seventeen hundred barrels of alcohol, and nine of them were empty.

beats.label: THEORY
beats.line: One theory says fumes caused a small blast, and the crew fled in panic.

beats.label: THE TWIST
beats.line: Captain Briggs, his wife, their two-year-old daughter and seven sailors were never seen again.

end.line: Would you have left the ship?

description: In December 1872 the Mary Celeste was found drifting in the Atlantic with food, cargo and the crew's belongings on board, but not a single person. Nobody knows why they left.

facts.claim: The Mary Celeste was found adrift and abandoned in the Atlantic on 4 December 1872 (ship's time), between the Azores and Portugal, by the Dei Gratia.
The ship carried ample provisions (about six months' worth) and the crew's belongings were still on board.
The single lifeboat was missing and the last log entry was dated 25 November 1872.
The cargo was 1,701 barrels of denatured alcohol; nine were found empty when unloaded in Genoa.
Ten people were aboard: Captain Benjamin Briggs, his wife Sarah, daughter Sophia (2), and seven crew; none were ever found.
One leading theory is that alcohol vapour caused a small explosion or scare, prompting a hasty abandonment.
